why: Rule 1: deg-4 junction with everything pointing away -- 9cm proton Bragg-rises monotonically to 14001, 391cm muon rises away to 14000, 97cm pi+ leaves toward 14008 where a 12cm proton stops at 14005; 14008 fails because its pi+ prong cools away from it.

Rule 1 clean 2-of-2 at a 110 degree kink: 67cm proton rises monotonically to a 230k Bragg at 20001 and the 167cm muon rises to a 190k stopping end at 20000, and the 28cm EM cluster 62 starts 3cm away.

Rule 1: the 55cm pi+ is cool at 10003 and hot at 10002 where a 147k 2cm proton stub sits, so 10002 is the stopping end; 10003 is also the lowest-z end and the two small blobs 26004/27006 flank it at 10cm.

Rule 1: both prongs of this 94 degree deg-2 junction get hotter away -- the 11cm proton Bragg-peaks at 210k on 2000 and the 21cm MIP ends in a bright spot at 2001; z favours 2001 by only 5cm, not enough to overturn it.

Three-prong apex: a 13cm proton rises to a 235k Bragg at 10001, and the principal-frame panel shows 10029 at the narrow end from which the other prongs fan out to 10000/10004/10005/10009; the high dQ/dx at 10029 is the vertex blob, not a Bragg.

Rule 1 at a deg-3 junction: 92cm proton Bragg-stops at 15002, 11cm proton Bragg-stops at 15005, 82cm muon leaves and stops at 15001 via 15004, plus the 43cm proton of cluster 23 starts 10cm away -- all pointing away.
Rules 1 and 7 agree: 11000 is the only deg-3 point, all three prongs rise away from it (18k at the apex to 40-87k at the tips), which is exactly a young EM shower opening from its conversion apex.

Rule 1 at a 79 degree junction: a 54cm proton rises monotonically along the template from 20k to 240k at 6003, starting exactly where the 520cm MIP track terminates at z=27, the most upstream point in the event.

The 158cm track is flat MIP end to end and the 68k-vs-52k end asymmetry is spike-driven, not monotone, so there is no Bragg and rule 1 is null; that leaves a genuine tie, broken by rule 2 toward the z=317 end 19001 over the z=461 end -- close to a guess.
Rule 1: the 89cm muon rises from MIP to a 210k Bragg at 12001, so it starts at 12000, where there is a vertex charge blob and a 7.6cm stub; the hot 5cm at 12000 is that blob, not a second Bragg.
Rule 1 topology at a 72 degree kink: a 16cm proton at 120k rising to 165k at 8004 branches off the 71cm MIP, with two sub-cm blobs 7-11cm away; the deg-4 alternative 8005 sits on the y=+200 face.
Fully contained 167cm track with a textbook stopping-muon Bragg at 8000 (180k falling over 15cm) and a 3.6cm Michel stub there, so by rules 1 and 3 the start is the cool, lowest-z end 8001.

The 85cm track is flat MIP with no Bragg, so the 195k point at 9002 with its 2.7cm 165k proton stub and half a dozen small blobs within 30cm is vertex activity; the other end 9001 sits on the z=0 face.

dQ/dx is continuous across 7004 (89.6k vs 88.8k, a hard proton scatter) but jumps at 7003 (100k proton vs 72k MIP), so 7003 joins two particles that stop at 7005 and 7001 -- both pointing away; the 150 degree prong pair costs a tier.

Rule 1: the contained 222cm MIP ends in an unmistakable Bragg rise to 455k at 16001 with a small blob 11cm off it, so the start is 16000, where the first 5cm carry a 210k vertex blob; low-z rule 2 loses to this.
